children: Iraq’s crude oil exports declined by more than 400,000 barrels per day (bpd) in September after climbing to their highest level since the eruption of the US-Iran conflict.
Iraq managed to boost crude exports to more than three million bpd in the first week of September, the highest level after the US-Iran war flared on February 28.

But exports averaged around 2.6 million bpd so far during the month, the oil ministry said in a statement on Monday.In its statement, the ministry said average oil exports through September is subject to the quantities expected to be exported in the remaining days of the month.

“This is considered a great achievement for the Ministry in reaching these export levels, under the current circumstances and the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz. This is part of the ministry’s keenness to sustain export operations at the highest possible quantity, to achieve the required financial revenues for the country’s public treasury,” the statement added.

Oil minister Bassim Khudair said in early September that crude exports surpassed three million bpd for the first time since the start of the US-Iran conflict, adding that they were no higher than 200,000 bpd when the government of prime minister Ali Al-Zaidi came to power in mid-May.
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)
